line: Lenovo Yoga Pro 9i Aura Edition Gen 10 (16" Intel, 2025)
config_name: Yoga Pro 9i Aura Edition Gen 10 — Core Ultra 9 285H, RTX 5060 8GB, 64GB LPDDR5X, 2TB SSD, 16" 3.2K Tandem OLED 120Hz

specs.cpu: Intel Core Ultra 9 285H (Arrow Lake-H, 16-core, P-cores up to 5.4GHz)
specs.keyboard_notes: Yoga creator keyboard; CNET noted slightly awkward keyboard placement

battery.notes: 84Wh (VERIFIED). RTX 5060 + Ultra 9 draw more under load; light-use similar to mid tier.

price.notes: CPU/GPU/RAM/storage options VERIFIED on PDP (Ultra 9 285H, RTX 5060, 64GB, 2TB). ld+json price hidden; estimated from CNET US$1,950 anchor + RTX 5060/64GB/2TB uplifts (~US$2,450 x 1.35).

reviews.quote: Centered around a gorgeous 16-inch OLED display, this Yoga laptop provides the performance and build that graphics pros demand.

praises: 64GB RAM handles 4K multi-cam timelines and local LLMs that 32GB tiers swap on
RTX 5060 in this chassis is ~15% faster in Blender/Resolve than the 5050 tier
Tandem OLED sustains 1,600-nit HDR highlights without the aggressive ABL of normal OLED
2TB Gen4 SSD built-in beats paying retail for a second drive later
Still ~1.6kg — lightest 16-inch dGPU creator laptop class
complaints: Steep config upcharges at Lenovo checkout; this tier approaches $3,300 CAD before eCoupons
RTX 5060 here is power-limited in the thin chassis — far from a full TDP desktop-class 5060
Tinny six-speaker array (CNET con) is a poor match for this price
64GB soldered is the ceiling; no 96/128GB option for heavy AI work
Fan noise under sustained GPU export is audible in quiet rooms

design_philosophy: The maxed-out expression of the Pro 9i formula: every option Lenovo offers on the 16-inch creator chassis — top CPU, upper RTX 50 tier, double RAM and storage — for professionals who treat the laptop as their primary workstation.
rating_notes: Inferred from CNET's reviewed Ultra 9 + RTX 5050 + 32GB/1TB config (8.6): +GPU tier → gaming +0.5, creative_work +0.5; 2x RAM → productivity +0.5, ai_ml +0.7; heavier sustained load → battery −0.3, thermals −0.2. CNET URL generic (exact slug unverified).
